mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% for two consecutive months signals central bank over-tightening, which raises real discount rates and reduces expected equity valuations, thereby depressing near-term S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% and remains above for ≥2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not fall below the 10th percentile of similar inflation spikes (p > 0.05) in walk-forward tests.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS exceeding 100,000 new jobs monthly indicates labor market strength, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain below the mean of prior labor-expansion periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO falling > 5% in a month) reflects weak manufacturing momentum, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >5% in a single month
failure_condition: 20 out-of-20 instances of INDPRO contractions do not precede negative 5-day forward returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in home prices (HOUST falling > 2% for three consecutive months) signals weakening household balance sheets, which raises perceived credit risk and dampens equity valuation, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by >2% for ≥3 consecutive months
failure_condition: During housing-cooling regimes, 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during housing-boom regimes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises above 4.5% for two consecutive months, the expectation of higher policy rates compresses the present value of future dividends, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.5% and remains above for ≥2 months
failure_condition: In high-rate normalization regimes, 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (UNRATE falling by >0.2 percentage points in one month) suggests strengthening labor market conditions, which elevates consumer spending and corporate optimism, yielding positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls by >0.2 pp in a single month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns do not exceed the 95th percentile of prior labor-tightening episodes (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining retail sales (not directly observable in the given catalog, but proxy via RSAFS falling > 10 million for two months) indicate waning consumer demand, which lowers earnings growth forecasts and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by >10 million for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During retail demand weakness regimes, 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during expansion (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in industrial production (INDPRO below 100 for three consecutive months) reflects structural supply-side constraints, reducing capacity utilization expectations and generating negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns during structural supply bottlenecks are not significantly worse than during normal conditions (p > 0.05).
